Definition: from G1519; inside (as preposition or adjective):-- (with-)in(-ner, -to, -ward).
BiblicalUsage: Ésō means inside — within, in the inner part. The inner man is renewed day by day, Paul says, even as the outward man perishes; and the disciples are shut inside the room when Jesus comes and stands among them. It is the word for the life within.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe ésō is the word for where the real work happens: the inner man, renewed daily, while the outward man fades. I hold that God cares most about the inside, and I should too.
RelatedEvents: The Resurrection; Jesus Appears to Thomas
